solution: By Vieta on \(x^2+\alpha x-\beta=0\): sum of roots \(\alpha+\beta=-\alpha\) and product \(\alpha\beta=-\beta\). From \(\alpha\beta=-\beta\): \(\beta(\alpha+1)=0\), and since \(\beta\neq0\) we get \(\alpha=-1\). Then \(\alpha+\beta=-\alpha\Rightarrow\beta=-2\alpha=2\). So \(\alpha=-1,\ \beta=2\). The expression becomes \(-x^2+\alpha x+\beta=-x^2-x+2\), a downward parabola with greatest value at \(x=-\tfrac{1}{2}\): \(-\tfrac14+\tfrac12+2=\tfrac94\). Hence greatest value \(\tfrac94\) — option D.

Let \(s=\alpha+\beta,\ p=\alpha\beta\). From \(\alpha\beta=\alpha^2\beta^2\): \(p=p^2\Rightarrow p=0\) or \(p=1\). From \(\alpha+\beta=\alpha^2+\beta^2=s^2-2p\): \(s=s^2-2p\). For \(p=0\): \(s^2-s=0\Rightarrow s=0,1\); for \(p=1\): \(s^2-s-2=0\Rightarrow s=2,-1\). This gives four valid \((s,p)\) pairs \((0,0),(1,0),(2,1),(-1,1)\), each a distinct quadratic \(x^2-sx+p=0\), and every one satisfies both relations (no distinct-root condition is imposed by the problem). Hence 4 equations — option D. [The old key B=2 wrongly discarded the two repeated-root cases.]

Expand along column 1: \(\det = x\,(1\cdot(-i)-i\cdot2i) + y\,\bigl(-(-3i\cdot(-i)-1\cdot2i)\bigr) = x(2-i)+y(3+2i)=(2x+3y)+i(-x+2y)\). Equate to \(6+11i\): \(2x+3y=6\) and \(-x+2y=11\). Solving, \(y=4,\ x=-3\). Hence \((x,y)=(-3,4)\) — option A. [Old key B was an arithmetic slip in solving the same correct system.]

Use \(\sin^{-1}x+\cos^{-1}x=\tfrac{\pi}{2}\). Subtract this from the given \(4\sin^{-1}x+\cos^{-1}x=\pi\): \(3\sin^{-1}x=\tfrac{\pi}{2}\Rightarrow\sin^{-1}x=\tfrac{\pi}{6}\), so \(\cos^{-1}x=\tfrac{\pi}{3}\). Then \(\sin^{-1}x+4\cos^{-1}x=\tfrac{\pi}{6}+\tfrac{4\pi}{3}=\tfrac{\pi}{6}+\tfrac{8\pi}{6}=\tfrac{9\pi}{6}=\tfrac{3\pi}{2}\) — option C. [Old solution had \(\sin^{-1}x\) and \(\cos^{-1}x\) swapped.]

Points on \(y^2=8x\): \((2t^2,4t)\). Distance-squared to \((4,2)\): \(D^2=(2t^2-4)^2+(4t-2)^2\). Then \(\dfrac{d(D^2)}{dt}=2(2t^2-4)(4t)+2(4t-2)(4)=16t^3-16=0\Rightarrow t^3=1\Rightarrow t=1\). Foot: \((2,4)\); minimum distance \(=\sqrt{(4-2)^2+(2-4)^2}=\sqrt{8}=2\sqrt2\) — option B. [Old solution's derivative \(4t^3-6t-2=0\) was wrong.]

For the trapezium with three equal sides of length 6 and base angle \(\alpha\), area \(A=36\sin\alpha(1+\cos\alpha)=36\bigl(\sin\alpha+\tfrac12\sin2\alpha\bigr)\). Then \(\dfrac{dA}{d\alpha}=36(\cos\alpha+\cos2\alpha)=0\Rightarrow 2\cos^2\alpha+\cos\alpha-1=0\Rightarrow(2\cos\alpha-1)(\cos\alpha+1)=0\Rightarrow\cos\alpha=\tfrac12\Rightarrow\alpha=\tfrac{\pi}{3}\) — option C. [Old solution dropped the \(\tfrac12\) on \(\sin2\alpha\).]

Let \(\theta\) be the angle with the floor. Top height \(h=5\sin\theta\) with \(\dfrac{dh}{dt}=-0.1\) m/s (sliding down). Differentiate: \(\dfrac{dh}{dt}=5\cos\theta\,\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}\). When the foot is \(4\) m away, \(\cos\theta=\tfrac45\), so \(-0.1=5\cdot\tfrac45\cdot\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}=4\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}\Rightarrow\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}=-0.025\) rad/s. The angle decreases at \(0.025\) rad/s — option D. [Old solution's equation was garbled.]

Line A: \(3y=10-4x\Rightarrow 4x+3y=10\). Line B: \(8x+6y+5=0\Rightarrow 4x+3y=-\tfrac52\). The two lines are parallel. Along a ray from O in direction \((\cos\phi,\sin\phi)\), with \(k=4\cos\phi+3\sin\phi\): \(OA=\tfrac{10}{k}\) and \(OB=\tfrac{-5/2}{k}\) (opposite signs, so O lies between A and B). Hence \(OA:OB=10:\tfrac52=4:1\) — option A. [Old key D=1:3 was wrong.]

Tangent-length-squared from \((x,y)\): to \(x^2+y^2+4x+3=0\) it is \(S_1=x^2+y^2+4x+3\); to \(x^2+y^2-6x+5=0\) it is \(S_2=x^2+y^2-6x+5\). Ratio \(2:3\Rightarrow\dfrac{S_1}{S_2}=\dfrac49\Rightarrow 9S_1=4S_2\): \(9(x^2+y^2+4x+3)=4(x^2+y^2-6x+5)\Rightarrow 5x^2+5y^2+60x+7=0\) — option D. [Old key A had \(-60x\); the sign is \(+60x\).]

Let \(x=\tfrac{ab}{cr},\ y=\tfrac{bc}{ar},\ z=\tfrac{ca}{br}\). Then \(xy=\tfrac{b^2}{r^2},\ yz=\tfrac{c^2}{r^2},\ zx=\tfrac{a^2}{r^2}\), so \(xy+yz+zx=\dfrac{a^2+b^2+c^2}{r^2}=1\). For positive \(x,y,z\) with \(xy+yz+zx=1\), \(\tan^{-1}x+\tan^{-1}y+\tan^{-1}z=\tfrac{\pi}{2}\) (the tangent of the sum has denominator \(1-(xy+yz+zx)=0\)). Hence the value is \(\tfrac{\pi}{2}\) — option A. [Old solution wrongly used \(x+y+z=xyz\).]

Put \(x^2=\cos2\theta\) (\(\theta\in(0,\tfrac{\pi}{4})\)). Then \(\sqrt{1+x^2}=\sqrt2\cos\theta\), \(\sqrt{1-x^2}=\sqrt2\sin\theta\), so the argument is \(\dfrac{\cos\theta+\sin\theta}{\cos\theta-\sin\theta}=\dfrac{1+\tan\theta}{1-\tan\theta}=\tan\!\bigl(\tfrac{\pi}{4}+\theta\bigr)\). Therefore the expression \(=\tfrac{\pi}{4}+\theta=\tfrac{\pi}{4}+\tfrac12\cos^{-1}x^2\) — option A. [Old solution skipped the key step.]

\(\tan^{-1}x+\tan^{-1}6x=\tfrac{\pi}{4}\Rightarrow\dfrac{7x}{1-6x^2}=1\Rightarrow 6x^2+7x-1=0\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{-7\pm\sqrt{73}}{12}\). Since \(\sqrt{73}\approx8.54\), the roots are \(\approx0.129\) and \(\approx-1.30\). Only the positive root satisfies \(x\ge0\) (and there \(1-6x^2>0\), so the sum is genuinely \(\tfrac{\pi}{4}\)). Thus A is a singleton set — option B. [Old key D claimed two elements; the negative root is excluded by \(x\ge0\).]

Over \([-1,1]\) the odd terms \(\dfrac{17x^5},\dfrac{29x^3},\dfrac{-31x}{}\) (odd numerator \(\div\) even denominator) integrate to 0. The even part is \(\dfrac{1-x^4}{x^2+1}=1-x^2\). So \(\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1}(1-x^2)\,dx=\Bigl[x-\tfrac{x^3}{3}\Bigr]_{-1}^{1}=\tfrac23-\left(-\tfrac23\right)=\tfrac43\) — option C. [Old solution slipped \(2\cdot\tfrac23=\tfrac45\); it equals \(\tfrac43\).]

\(A(\operatorname{adj}A)=(\det A)I\). Expanding, \(\det A=x(yz-8)-3(z-8)+2(2-2y)=xyz-8x-4y-3z+28\). Substitute \(xyz=60\) and \(8x+4y+3z=20\): \(\det A=60-20+28=68\). Hence \(A(\operatorname{adj}A)=68I\) — option D. [Old key C=20I used only \(8x+4y+3z\) and dropped the \(xyz\) and \(+28\) terms.]

\(x\to0^+\): \(\dfrac{x}{x+x^2}=\dfrac{1}{1+x}\to1\). \(x\to0^-\): \(\dfrac{-x}{-x+x^2}=\dfrac{1}{1-x}\to1\). Both one-sided limits equal 1, so the limit is \(1\) — option B. [The stored solution itself derived 1; only the key letter was wrong.]

\(0/0\) at \(x=0\); apply L'Hopital. Numerator derivative: \(\tfrac13(27-2x)^{-2/3}(-2)\to\tfrac13\cdot\tfrac19\cdot(-2)=-\tfrac{2}{27}\). Denominator derivative: \(-3\cdot\tfrac15(243+5x)^{-4/5}\cdot5=-3(243+5x)^{-4/5}\to-3\cdot\tfrac{1}{81}=-\tfrac{1}{27}\) (since \(243^{4/5}=3^4=81\)). Limit \(=\dfrac{-2/27}{-1/27}=2\) — option C. [Old key A=\tfrac23 was an arithmetic slip; the steps give 2.]

The quadratic \(ax^2+bx+1\) applies where \(|2x-3|\ge2\) (i.e. \(x\le\tfrac12\) or \(x\ge\tfrac52\)); the line \(3x+2\) on \((\tfrac12,\tfrac52)\). Continuity at \(x=\tfrac12\): \(\tfrac{a}{4}+\tfrac{b}{2}+1=\tfrac72\Rightarrow a+2b=10\). At \(x=\tfrac52\): \(\tfrac{25a}{4}+\tfrac{5b}{2}+1=\tfrac{19}{2}\Rightarrow 25a+10b=34\). Solving: \(5a+10b=50\) so \(20a=-16\Rightarrow a=-\tfrac45\), \(b=\tfrac{27}{5}\). Then \(a+b=-\tfrac45+\tfrac{27}{5}=\tfrac{23}{5}\) — option C. [Old key A=\tfrac{13}{5} applied continuity at only one point.]
